newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav Trepca signs $135 mln export deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav Trepca signs $135 mln export deal - paper.

text.p: The Yugoslav metals giant Trepca of Kosovska Mitrovica and the Greek Mitilineos company have concluded a $135 million export deal, the Belgrade daily Borba reported on Wednesday.

Under the agreement, signed on Tuesday by Trepca general manager Novak Bjelic and the Greek company owner Evangelos Mitilineos, Trepca will deliver metals and other products to the Greek partner over a period of two years.
No-one at Trepca was immediately available for comment.

Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca, based in Serbia's southern province of Kosovo, is the country's largest metals complex, employing some 12,000 people, and includes 14 lead and zinc mines plus metallurgical plants.
The two companies first signed a deal worth $51 million last December, shortly after sanctions against rump Yugoslavia were suspended.

Under that deal Trepca has already delivered $18 million worth of lead and zinc, and plans to export another $15 million worth of its products by the end of the year. The ballance is to be exported in 1997.
Mitilineos has deposited some $30 million in advance payments into Trepca's account, Borba quoted Bjelic as saying.
"Without such financial support Trepca would certainly not have been able to restart production and revitalise its installations," Bjelic said.
Trepca plans to raise annual production to $500 million by the year 2000, of which around $300 million would be exported.
